_meta.purpose: Research for a London Travel Geek section on drinking around Wembley Stadium and OVO Arena Wembley on an event day: (1) whether shops near the stadium are barred from selling alcohol on event days, and in what legal form; (2) where you can actually drink nearby and what each place does on an event day.
_meta.sourceRule: Council, legislation, venue and operator sources only. Brent Council pages and documents, legislation.gov.uk, wembleystadium.com and its help portal, ovoarena.co.uk, wembleypark.com (Quintain, the estate operator), and each pub, bar or retailer's own site. Archived copies of Brent's own pages (web.archive.org) are used only to show what Brent itself published on past football days. No forums, listicles or fan blogs are relied on; one fan site is recorded under folkloreCheck as evidence, not as a source.
methodNotes: Walking times are TfL Journey Planner API results (mode=walking, shortest journey returned) from each venue's postcode centroid (postcodes.io) to the centroid of HA9 0WS (Wembley Stadium) and HA9 0AA (OVO Arena). Postcode centroids can sit 50-150 m from the actual door, so treat every figure as plus or minus 2 minutes. Where an operator publishes its own walking time it is recorded alongside, and conflicts are flagged.

PSPO coverage was tested by point-in-polygon against Brent's own map layer for the Wembley Park PSPO (https://www.brent.gov.uk/-/media/maps/external/wembley_park_pspo.json), the file Brent's PSPO map loads. The boundary is Brent's; the in/out calls are mine from their data.
Brent's licensing policy was read from the PDF linked on Brent's 'Licences and permits' page. Page numbers are the PDF's printed page numbers.

headlineAnswer.claimTested: You cannot buy alcohol from the supermarkets and shops around Wembley on match days or gig days.
headlineAnswer.verdict: Not true as a blanket statement, and no official source says it. There is no borough-wide or area-wide ban on shops selling alcohol on event days, statutory or voluntary. What does exist has three separate legal shapes, and people run them together.
theThreeThingsThatActuallyExist: 1. LICENCE CONDITIONS (statutory, but premises-by-premises). Brent's Statement of Licensing Policy 2025-2030, Policy 9, says the council imposes 'special conditions in Wembley' for major event days, including no alcohol sales in the hour before an event, no off-sales to anyone wearing 'game day paraphernalia', and a four-can limit. Where a condition is on a licence it is legally binding on that shop or pub. But the policy's own appendix says these conditions are considered only 'where there is a relevant representation', which means they are attached case by case when a licence is granted, varied or reviewed. They are not automatically on every licence, and Brent does not publish which licences carry them.

2. A STREET-DRINKING ORDER (statutory, but about drinking, not selling). The Wembley Park Public Spaces Protection Order, in force from 1 February 2026 to 31 January 2029, lets a police officer, PCSO or council officer make you stop drinking in a public place and surrender your alcohol, including sealed containers. Refusing is an offence: GBP 100 fixed penalty, up to GBP 500 on prosecution. Brent publicises this as a 'No Street Drinking Zone' on named big events. It does not restrict sales at all.

3. A CUMULATIVE IMPACT POLICY (statutory, but about new licences). Wembley Park and Wembley Central are Cumulative Impact Zones where new off-licences, or variations that increase sales, are presumed refused. Brent states existing licences are not affected. It has nothing to do with event days.
headlineAnswer.howToPutItToReaders: Shops near the stadium are licensed to sell alcohol and there is no general event-day ban. Some licences carry Brent's event-day conditions, so a shop may refuse to sell in the hour before an event, refuse anyone in team colours, or cap you at four cans. And even if you do buy, you cannot drink it on the street: officers can take it off you under the PSPO, sealed cans included.
headlineAnswer.whatWouldBeWrongToPrint: 'You can't buy alcohol in Wembley on event days' overstates it. 'Some shops choose not to sell' understates it, because for some premises it is a licence condition, not a choice. The accurate position is: event-day sales restrictions exist as conditions on individual licences, not as a blanket rule.

licensingPolicyEventDayConditions.legalForm: Statutory, via conditions on individual premises licences under the Licensing Act 2003. Brent is the licensing authority. Breaching a licence condition is carrying on a licensable activity other than in accordance with the licence, which is a criminal offence.
licensingPolicyEventDayConditions.document: London Borough of Brent, Statement of Licensing Policy 2025 - 2030

policy9.location: Policy 9: Impact of major entertainment venues, page 22
policy9.policyStatement_verbatim: The council will continue the policy of imposing special conditions in Wembley for dealing with alcohol-related issues during major events.
conditionsListed_verbatim: No sale of alcohol one hour before the event, and one hour after.
No alcohol to be sold off-licence to those wearing game day paraphernalia.
Customers shall not be allowed to congregate outside the premises.
No glass bottles shall be handed over the bar but shall be decanted into plastic vessels.
The DPS shall work in partnership with the Police and comply with any direction given by the most senior Police Office on duty at the event.
No alcohol of `alcopop' type drinks shall be displayed or sold in glass containers with the exception of wines and spirits.
No more than 4 cans of alcohol can be sold to a customer.

appendixVersion.location: Appendix section 'Major events at Wembley Stadium', pages 39-40 (listed in the contents at page 40)
appendixVersion.trigger_verbatim: During major events at Wembley Stadium the following recommended conditions will be considered where there is a relevant representation:
conditionsListed_verbatim: No sale of alcohol one hour before the event.
Customers shall not be allowed to congregate outside the premises.
No glass bottles shall be handed over the bar but shall be decanted into plastic vessels.
The DPS shall work in partnership with the Police and comply with any direction given by the most senior Police Office on duty at the event.
No alcohol of `alcopop' type drinks shall be displayed or sold in glass containers with the exception of wines and spirits.
No more than 4 cans of alcohol shall be sold per customer.
appendixVersion.differenceFromPolicy9: The appendix list drops both 'and one hour after' and the 'game day paraphernalia' off-licence condition. The policy contradicts itself, and it does not say which list governs.

whatThisMeansInPractice: It is a menu of conditions Brent applies to Wembley premises when their licence comes before it, not a rule that switches on for every shop on every event day.

The 'game day paraphernalia' condition is aimed at off-licences, meaning any premises selling for consumption off the premises. That would include a supermarket or a convenience store if its licence carries it. In practice it means a fan in a team shirt can be refused even where nobody else is.

The police-direction condition is how a police request to stop selling becomes enforceable. For a premises whose licence carries it, a direction from the senior officer on duty is binding. For a premises without it, a police request is only a request, unless the police obtain a court closure order (see section160ClosureOrders).
licensingPolicyEventDayConditions.doesItApplyToEveryEvent: Not stated. Policy 9 says 'major events' and 'major event days'; the appendix says 'major events at Wembley Stadium'. Neither defines a major event or says whether OVO Arena shows count. The one pub that publishes its own conditions, The White Horse, applies its sales cut-off to football matches only and not to stadium concerts (see questionTwo).
licensingPolicyEventDayConditions.whichPremises: Premises 'in Wembley' (no boundary given in the policy). Only those whose licences actually carry the conditions.
licensingPolicyEventDayConditions.hours: Policy 9: one hour before the event and one hour after. Appendix: one hour before the event. 'One hour after' is not defined as after the start or after the end. The White Horse describes its own version as stopping sales one hour before kick-off until 15 minutes after kick-off.
licensingPolicyEventDayConditions.supermarketsOffLicencesPetrolStations: The policy draws no distinction between them. Each condition binds whatever premises it is written onto. The paraphernalia condition is framed around off-sales, so it is the one that bites on shops. No petrol station was identified inside the zone during this check.

pspoStreetDrinking.legalForm: Statutory. Public Spaces Protection Order made under section 59 of the Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014. It controls CONSUMPTION in public places. It contains nothing about the sale of alcohol.
pspoStreetDrinking.order: Brent Council Public Spaces Protection Order (Borough Wide, Parks Open Spaces Cemeteries and Graveyards, and Wembley Park), made 30 January 2026, in force from 12:01 on 1 February 2026 to 11:59 on 31 January 2029. Made by Nigel Chapman, Corporate Director for Children, Young People and Community Development.

alcoholProhibition_verbatim.heading: Consumption of alcohol in a public place to cause alarm, distress or harassment
alcoholProhibition_verbatim.text: Any person(s) who intend(s) to, is or has been consuming alcohol, without reasonable excuse. This person must: a. cease the consumption of alcohol immediately b. surrender any alcohol that the authorised officer reasonably believes to be, alcohol or a container for alcohol (this includes any sealed containers). c. A reasonable excuse includes: i. an area adjoining a premises which is licensed to supply and permit the consumption of alcohol. ii. Another licensed area where alcohol consumption is permitted.

notes: The same alcohol clause appears in all three restricted areas: borough-wide, parks, and Wembley Park. Street drinking is therefore controllable anywhere in Brent, not just at Wembley.
The heading mentions 'alarm, distress or harassment' but the operative text does not. As written, it covers anyone consuming alcohol in a public place without reasonable excuse.

Sealed cans can be taken: the order says so expressly. Brent's licensing policy (Policy 12, page 23) still describes the older wording 'other than a sealed container'. The 2026 order is the operative text.
A pub's own terrace or beer garden is a 'reasonable excuse' under the order.
pspoStreetDrinking.penalties: Failing to comply with the alcohol requirement: Fixed Penalty Notice GBP 100, payable within 14 days, or a fine up to level 2 (GBP 500) on prosecution. Source: the order and Brent's PSPO page.
pspoStreetDrinking.whenItApplies: The order has no event-day limit. It is in force at all times for its three-year life. What changes on event days is enforcement. Brent says it and its partners 'are enforcing a No Street Drinking Zone on Olympic Way and the surrounding area' during named events.

namedEventsOnBrentsPage2026.wording: Enforced 'during a number of big music concerts and showcase sporting events at Wembley Stadium this year'.
namedEventsOnBrentsPage2026.notListedAsOf10Sep: England v Spain (26 Sep), the Union Jack Classic (19 Sep), England v Czechia (6 Oct), the NFL game (18 Oct) and England v Croatia (12 Nov) do not appear yet. Past practice (below) shows Brent adds football fixtures to the page closer to the date.

stadiumsVersion.summary: The stadium says Brent and its partners have enforced the no-street-drinking zone on Olympic Way and the surrounding area for ALL events at the stadium since 2022. Fans drinking there will be asked to hand over alcohol and may face enforcement. It points fans to licensed bars, pubs and restaurants instead.

pspoStreetDrinking.conflict: Brent says named events; the stadium says all events. Both describe enforcement of an order that legally applies at all times, so the safe line for readers is that street drinking can be stopped on any day, and is actively policed on event days.

areaCovered.boundaryAsDescribedInTheOrder: Wembley Park restricted area: from Wembley Stadium station along the railway to Hannah Close, then the railway up to Bridge Road; up to the first section of Forty Avenue and Forty Lane; back down via Empire Way, Wembley Hill Road and Wembley Park Drive to Park Lane, including King Edward VII Park; down to High Road, Wembley; along Harrow Road one way to the junction with Napier Road and the other way to the junction with Berkhamsted Avenue; including the first section of Oakington Manor Drive; and back to the railway at Wembley Stadium station. The map also takes in the first sections of some side roads, such as Brook Avenue by Wembley Park station.
areaCovered.radius: None. It is a drawn area, not a radius.
areaCovered.extentFromBrentsMapLayer: Bounding box roughly longitude -0.3039 to -0.2568, latitude 51.5438 to 51.5661.
areaCovered.venuesTestedInside: Every venue and shop in this file tested inside the Wembley Park area, from J.J. Moon's on the High Road to The Torch by Wembley Park station, the Green Man on Dagmar Avenue and the Corner House on Harrow Road. In practice the whole walk between any of these pubs and the stadium is inside the zone.
areaCovered.boroughWideToo: The borough-wide area carries the same alcohol clause, so leaving the Wembley Park zone does not take you outside the rule.

otherWembleyParkProhibitionsReadersWillM: Stadium concourse: no entering or remaining on the concourse around gates A-M without a valid ticket for that day's event.
No ticket touting, unlicensed street trading or unlicensed merchandise selling.
No pyrotechnics, flares or smoke devices; no drones without landowner consent.

cumulativeImpactZones.legalForm: Statutory. Cumulative Impact Policy under the Licensing Act 2003 (section 5A), set out in the licensing policy (Policy 11 and Appendix 6).
cumulativeImpactZones.effect: Brent's page says the Cumulative Impact Policy applies only to off-licences. Applications for new off-licences, or variations that would increase alcohol sales including longer hours, are presumed refused unless the applicant shows no negative cumulative impact. Existing licence holders are not affected unless they apply to vary in a way that adds impact. The policy (page 23) adds that the zones 'will not cause any existing licences to be changed'.

wembleyZones.wembleyPark: From the junction of Barn Rise and Forty Avenue to Wembley Triangle: Empire Way, South Way, Wembley Hill Road, Engineers Way, Grand Parade (Forty Avenue), Olympic Way, Bridge Road, Wembley Park Drive.
wembleyZones.wembleyCentral: North of the North Circular to Talbot Road: High Road, Lancelot Road, Harrow Road (Wembley, north of the North Circular), London Road, Central Square, Wembley Park Drive.

cumulativeImpactZones.whyItMatters: The evidence base (policy page 53) notes the areas immediately around the stadium and arena are again a crime hotspot since events returned after Covid. That is a reason Brent limits new off-licences there. It is not an event-day sales ban.

section160ClosureOrders.legalForm: Statutory. Licensing Act 2003, section 160, still in force.
section160ClosureOrders.whatItAllows: Where there is or is expected to be disorder, a magistrates' court may order all premises with a premises licence or temporary event notice at or near the place to close for up to 24 hours. Only a police officer of superintendent rank or above can apply, and only if closure is necessary to prevent disorder. This covers shops and pubs alike.
section160ClosureOrders.found: No Brent, Met, stadium or operator source found that says such an order has been made for a Wembley event. This is the only route by which every licensed premises in an area could lawfully be shut on a given fixture.

voluntarySchemes.found: Brent's policy encourages voluntary measures: Policy 15 (a voluntary ban on high-strength alcohol) and Policy 20 (voluntary schemes such as Pubwatch). Both are borough-wide and aimed at street drinking. Neither is an event-day agreement.
voluntarySchemes.eventDayVoluntaryAgreement: No voluntary event-day agreement between Brent, the Met and local retailers was found in any Brent, Met, stadium, arena, Quintain or retailer source.

folkloreCheck.summary: The only place a blanket 'off-licences stop selling' rule turned up in any search was a fan site, euro2028fan.com. None of its specifics match Brent's documents.

item.dated: 18 June 2026, billed as a one-minute read
item.claims: That Brent has 'confirmed' a EURO 2028 regime: a 1.2 km PSPO radius from 11:00 to 02:00 on every matchday, and off-licences in the zone stopping sales two hours before kick-off.
item.whyItIsNotCredible: The sealed PSPO has no radius and no hours. The licensing policy says one hour, not two. The piece attributes everything to Brent with no link or document. It fits the content-farm pattern.
searchesItWasTheSoleAnswerTo: Wembley stadium event day shops not selling alcohol police request
Metropolitan Police Wembley stadium event day alcohol dispersal order

folkloreCheck.likelyOriginOfTheBelief: The genuine 'no off-sales to those wearing game day paraphernalia' condition, together with PSPO confiscations of sealed cans, would feel to a fan like 'the shops won't sell to you'. That is plausible but is my inference, not a sourced fact.

whatCouldNotBeEstablished: WHICH shops carry the event-day conditions. Brent's online register shows permitted hours but not licence conditions. It also only surfaces the first 50 of 1,058 current licences and ignores its own street filter, so it cannot even list every off-licence near the stadium.
Whether Tesco Wembley Stadium Express, Sainsbury's Local (Civic Centre) or the Co-op on Olympic Way have any event-day condition on their licences.
What counts as a 'major event' for the conditions, whether OVO Arena shows count, and what 'one hour after' means.

Any Metropolitan Police event-day advice on alcohol. met.police.uk refuses automated access and two searches surfaced nothing from the Met. Brent lists the Met's Brent licensing mailbox (NWMailbox.LicensingBrent@met.police.uk) as a responsible authority.
Any instance of a section 160 closure order, or a documented police request to shops, for a Wembley fixture.
Any published event-day notice from Sainsbury's (its own store page was not found).

howFootballDaysWork.summary: On football days Brent publishes which pubs are hosting which fans, split by the side of the stadium your ticket is on. Pubs near the ground often admit only ticket holders for their allocated team. For concerts there is no allocation.
howFootballDaysWork.brentsWording: Brent's archived match-day pages list venues 'including which ones are hosting which fans' and group them by stadium side.
howFootballDaysWork.theWhiteHorseConfirms: The White Horse's football page tells fans of the team not allocated to it to check Brent's event-days page for the pubs, venues and fan zones allocated to their team.

wembleyStadium.alcoholOnSale: Yes. Draught bars and bottle bars on the general-admission levels 1 and 5. Level 2 has TapHouse Social, Camden Town Brewery bars and two M&S Food stores, open to level-2 ticket holders only. The stadium is cashless.

rulesByEventType.rugbyLeagueAndAmericanFootball: Permitted. That covers the Union Jack Classic (19 Sep 2026) and the NFL game (18 Oct 2026).
rulesByEventType.englandFriendliesFaCupFootballLeague: Permitted on concourses and in restaurants and private hospitality.
rulesByEventType.competitiveUefaAndFifaFixtures: Only in restaurants and private hospitality areas. Not on the public concourses, which includes anyone with a block number starting 1 or 5.
rulesByEventType.allFootball: No alcohol may be consumed in the main bowl or within view of the pitch, including at the FA Cup Final, semi-finals and other cup finals.

wembleyStadium.thisAutumnsEnglandGames: England v Spain (26 Sep), England v Czechia (6 Oct) and England v Croatia (12 Nov), all 19:45, are all UEFA Nations League fixtures on the stadium's own event pages. Under the stadium's rule that means no alcohol on the level 1 and level 5 concourses at any of them.
wembleyStadium.groundRegulations: Regulation 15 cites the Sporting Events (Control of Alcohol etc) Act 1985. It is an offence to try to enter, or to be inside, while drunk. It is also an offence to have alcohol, or a bottle, can or similar container, when entering or in a public area from which the event can be directly viewed. Arrest and a banning order are possible.
wembleyStadium.bringYourOwn: No food or drink may be brought in from outside. 'Alcohol, food & drink (except permitted items)' is on the restricted list, as are cans, flasks, and glass, hard-plastic and metal bottles. The only exception is one empty, crushable, clear plastic bottle of up to 500 ml without a lid, in seated areas only, for filling at the free water stations. For concerts, bottles are not allowed in pitch standing areas.

ovoArenaWembley.alcoholOnSale: Yes. Concourse kiosks sell cocktails, spirits and mixers, wine and prosecco, craft beer, lager and cider. The premium lounges serve the same range. Cashless. Selected food and drink can be ordered through the arena app for collection.
ovoArenaWembley.idPolicy: Challenge 25: anyone who looks under 25 should expect to show photo ID to buy alcohol.
ovoArenaWembley.bringYourOwn: You may bring confectionery but no drinks. Alcohol may not be brought in; it is sold at the bars inside. Glass, cans, aluminium bottles and flasks are refused. At standing events all reusable drinks bottles are prohibited.
ovoArenaWembley.readmission: None. Anyone who leaves, including to smoke, cannot come back in.
ovoArenaWembley.viewOfStage: The arena publishes no rule restricting drinking in view of the stage or in the auditorium.

Stops selling alcohol from one hour before kick-off until 15 minutes after kick-off. The pub says it is required to do this, among several additions to its licence for football days. A bell rings 20 minutes before the cut-off.

Pre-stadium dining is in the first-floor restaurant, for groups of up to six, for up to 90 minutes, with a main course per head required. Booking is recommended and tables are released after 15 minutes.

Opens at noon, earlier for early kick-offs. Under-18s usually admitted until 20:00. ID for anyone who looks under 25, and bag searches.

traditionalPubsWithinWalkingDistance.walkToStadium: 15 min (TfL); 10 min to the arena. The pub's own site says its car park is 300 m from the stadium. That looks optimistic against TfL's figure and should be checked before printing.
traditionalPubsWithinWalkingDistance.what: Pub, restaurant and large beer garden; big-screen sport. Its own site says it is known for a lively atmosphere on concert and match days, with a barbecue on match days.
traditionalPubsWithinWalkingDistance.eventDay: No entry charge, ticketing or fan restriction is published. It sells event-day parking: GBP 40 for stadium events and GBP 20 for arena events, car park open from 08:00, book by phone and pay on arrival. Those prices are PARKING, not pub entry.
traditionalPubsWithinWalkingDistance.dataWarning: An older site, thegreenmanhotelatwembley.co.uk, is frozen at 2015 and has spam injected into it. Do not use it.

gapsForRob.gap: Which shops' licences carry Brent's event-day conditions
gapsForRob.whyItMatters: This decides whether a named supermarket can legally sell to a fan in team colours, or in the hour before kick-off. The online register cannot answer it: it shows hours, not conditions.
gapsForRob.howToSettle: Ask Brent licensing (business.licence@brent.gov.uk) for the conditions on the premises licences of Tesco Wembley Stadium Express (20 Wembley Park Boulevard), Sainsbury's Local (Brent Civic Centre), Co-op (25 Olympic Way) and Capitol Food & Wine (107 Wembley Park Drive).

gapsForRob.gap: What 'major event' means in Policy 9, and which list governs
gapsForRob.whyItMatters: The policy's two lists differ: the paraphernalia condition and 'one hour after' are only in Policy 9. Neither says whether arena shows or concerts count.

gapsForRob.gap: Whether the No Street Drinking Zone is enforced at every event or only named ones
gapsForRob.whyItMatters: The stadium says all events since 2022. Brent names specific events, and as of 10 September its list has no football fixtures. The order itself applies at all times, so the reader line 'you can be made to hand over alcohol on any day' is safe either way.
gapsForRob.howToSettle: Re-check Brent's event-days page in the week of England v Spain (26 Sep); past football days show Brent adds fixtures and pub allocations closer to the date.

gapsForRob.detail: Nothing found from the Met. Its site refuses automated access, and two searches surfaced only the fan site noted under folkloreCheck.
gapsForRob.howToSettle: Check the Met's Brent social channels on a match week, or ask the Met's Brent licensing mailbox, which Brent lists as a responsible authority.

gapsForRob.gap: Event-day policies of Feed the Yak, the Green Man, J.J. Moon's, the Torch and the independents
gapsForRob.detail: None publishes one. Brent's allocation lists are the only official evidence of how they operate on football days.
gapsForRob.howToSettle: Phone them in the week of a match, or print the Brent-allocation rule rather than venue-by-venue claims.

gapsForRob.detail: The pub says its car park is 300 m from the stadium; TfL routes 15 minutes from its postcode.
gapsForRob.howToSettle: Walk or map it before printing a figure.

gapsForRob.detail: Not found, so there is no retailer-side check for Sainsbury's. Tesco's and Co-op's pages carry no event-day notice.
